_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:09:05Z)**_

I'd keep it. Supporting the handle drag turns out to be a small change, and it lets us remove the special case we added.

**What I found:** the resize code already works out whether a handle drag has flipped the shape. It computes `flipByX` by comparing against the shape as it was when the drag started, for single shapes ([resizeElements.ts:166](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts#L166)) and for multi-selections ([resizeElements.ts:1137](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts#L1137)). Shift+H also goes through that same multi-selection resize code with `flipByX: true` ([actionFlip.ts:131-150](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFlip.ts#L131-L150)).

**The change:** move the colour swap out of `actionFlip` and into those two resize spots. While the shape is flipped it gets the mirrored gradient; otherwise it keeps its original one, both worked out from the starting shape.

- **Both ways of flipping work**, because Shift+H, right-click → Flip and handle drags all run through the resize code.
- **No double swaps while dragging back and forth.** Each mouse move recalculates from the original shape, so dragging past the edge and back returns the original colours.
- **One place instead of two:** the code we added to `actionFlip` in step 5 would be deleted.

**Dropping it instead:**

- **Upside:** it's the simplest option. Revert step 5, and #67's answer to its open question becomes "a gradient stays in the shape's own orientation; flipping doesn't change it". That's a defensible definition of "consistent".
- **Downside 1:** acceptance criterion A then rests on that definition, and you'd want to write it into the issue so reviewers know it was intentional.
- **Downside 2:** users would have to swap the colours manually. The picker has no swap button, so that means re-picking both the start and end colours.

The resize version is about the same amount of code as step 5 and fixes what you're seeing. Want me to go ahead with it?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:15:40Z)**_

Yes, that's exactly why it happens:

- **What flipping changes:** only the shape's geometry. For lines and freedraw that means mirroring their points; for other shapes, their position and angle. That's all [resizeElements.ts](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts) changes, whether you flip with a handle drag or with Shift+H.
- **Where the gradient lives:** it's stored as text in `backgroundColor`, for example `linear-gradient(90deg, black, white)`. It's always drawn left→right along the shape's own axis, so a geometry flip never touches it. After flipping, the shape is mirrored but the gradient still runs black→white from the shape's left side.
- **What step 5 adds:** a colour swap in `backgroundColor`, but only inside the Flip horizontal action (Shift+H / right-click). The handle drag goes straight through the resize code and never reaches that swap.

For the PR's known-limitation line, you could phrase it that way:

> Flipping only mirrors an element's geometry; the gradient is stored in `backgroundColor` and isn't geometry, so it has to be swapped explicitly. Flip horizontal (Shift+H / context menu) does this. Flipping by dragging a resize handle past the opposite edge doesn't yet.

If you meant that Shift+H also isn't mirroring the gradient in your browser, tell me. That would be a different problem, since the tests say it works.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:16:40Z)**_

No. The commit didn't add the behaviour you're seeing; it's how Excalidraw already worked. And the "visual flip" you're describing is what step 5 already does, but only for one of the two ways to flip.

- **Flipping the geometry** is stock Excalidraw. [actionFlip.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFlip.ts) and [resizeElements.ts](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts) mirrored shapes long before #65 or #67.
- **Step 5, commit `c1a196bd`,** added exactly your "visual flip": it swaps the gradient's start and end colours, so black→white becomes white→black and the shape looks mirrored. But it lives only in the Flip horizontal action ([actionFlip.ts:196-203](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFlip.ts#L196-L203)), so it only runs for Shift+H and right-click → Flip horizontal.
- **Handle-drag flips** skip that action and go straight through the resize code, so the colours aren't swapped. That's the case you tested.

| How you flip | Shape mirrors | Gradient start/end swap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shift+H / right-click → Flip horizontal | ✅ | ✅ (step 5) |
| Drag a resize handle past the opposite edge | ✅ | ❌ |

If you want the handle drag to do the visual flip too, that's the resize-code change I described earlier. You decided it wasn't worth it inside #67, so it's currently recorded as a known limitation. Either outcome is fine: leave it for a follow-up, or add it now. Your call.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:36:41Z)**_

Step 5 is revised: every way of flipping now mirrors the gradient. That covers Shift+H, right-click → Flip horizontal, and dragging a resize handle past the opposite edge, for single shapes and multi-selections. The full suite passes (117 of 117 files, 1,607 tests), along with typecheck, eslint (zero warnings) and prettier, and no snapshot files changed.

**What changed:**

- **[resizeElements.ts](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts):** the colour swap now lives in the resize code that every flip goes through, instead of the Flip action.
  - **[Line 889](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts#L889), single-shape drags (`resizeSingleElement`):** if the shape has a linear gradient, it gets the mirrored colours while it's flipped (`nextWidth < 0`) and its original colours otherwise.
  - **[Line 1447](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts#L1447), multi-selections and Shift+H (`resizeMultipleElements`):** the same rule, using the existing `flipByX`. It mirrors how that function already flips images (`scale`) a few lines above. A new `backgroundColor` field on the update type is at [line 1357](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts#L1357), and the import is at [line 63](packages/element/src/resizeElements.ts#L63).
  - **Why dragging back and forth is safe:** both spots calculate from the shape as it was when the drag started, never from its current colours. Dragging past the edge and back within one drag lands on the original colours, with no double swaps.
- **[actionFlip.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFlip.ts):** the step 5 swap and its import are removed. The file is now identical to before step 5, since Shift+H gets the swap from the resize code.
- **[gradient.test.tsx:493](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx#L493):** 6 new tests for flipping by handle drag:

  - dragging past the opposite edge mirrors the gradient;
  - resizing without crossing the edge keeps it;
  - dragging past and back in one drag restores it;
  - a vertical drag-flip leaves it unchanged;
  - a closed line dragged by its corner handle mirrors;
  - a multi-selection dragged past its edge mirrors every shape.

  The original Shift+H tests still pass unchanged.

One test-side note: dragging a line by its side (`e`) handle didn't register in the test environment, so the line test uses the corner (`se`) handle. Side handles on lines are worth a quick check in your browser.

Staging for the combined step 5 + 6 commit, adding the two new files and the updated test file to what's already staged:
